summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (sets, binomial counting, permutations, induction, graphs, the union bound, and elementary number theory with gcd, primes, modular inverses and the Chinese remainder theorem), an algorithms course (asymptotic notation, recurrences and geometric sums, divide and conquer including Karatsuba, sorting including radix sort, stacks, amortized counters, the RAM model and worst-case running time), and an introductory theory course with Turing machines and multitape tapes. From computer organization they know binary and two's-complement encodings, bit order, XOR and binary arithmetic; from calculus and a first linear-algebra course they know logarithms, exponentials, Newton's method, simple inequalities, complex numbers with conjugates, polynomials, matrices, Gaussian elimination, rank, dot products, projections and eigenvalues over the real or rational numbers. They have not studied abstract algebra (rings, quotient rings, finite fields, tensor products, bilinear forms over 𝔽₂), Fourier analysis, numerical error analysis, or the research literature on fast integer multiplication, so the FFT machinery, resampling and all of the paper's constructions are new to them.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a string of bits (or digits in base 2^b) whose positions carry powers of the base, so a k-bit string encodes a value in [0, 2^k).

known.name: Two's-complement representation
known.gloss: The fixed-width encoding of a signed integer N in w bits as N mod 2^w, so the range is [−2^{w−1}, 2^{w−1}), negation is complement-and-increment, and widening copies the sign bit.

known.name: Bit order and endianness
known.gloss: The convention fixing whether a stored binary word lists its most significant or least significant bit first, so that reversing a word converts one order into the other.

known.name: Bitwise exclusive or
known.gloss: The bitwise operation that outputs 1 exactly where its two input bits differ, so x ⊕ y ⊕ y = x and XOR is its own inverse.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The number of nonzero entries (ones) in a binary vector or string.

known.name: Logarithms and exponent rules
known.gloss: The inverse of exponentiation, with log(ab) = log a + log b, change of base log_m x = log x / log m, and the conventions lg for base two and log for base e.

known.name: Floor, ceiling and rounding
known.gloss: The maps sending a real number to the greatest integer below it, the least integer above it, the nearest integer, or the integer obtained by dropping its fractional part.

known.name: Worst-case running time
known.gloss: The maximum number of steps an algorithm takes over all inputs of a given length, viewed as a function of that length.

known.name: RAM model of computation
known.gloss: The machine model in which each memory word can be read or written at any address in one step, used for most algorithm analysis in contrast to sequential-access tapes.

known.name: Recurrences and recursion trees
known.gloss: Bounding the cost of a recursive algorithm by an inequality such as F(e) ≤ a·F(e/m) + overhead and summing the work level by level over the recursion tree.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: The sum 1 + a + … + a^k = (a^{k+1} − 1)/(a − 1), which is dominated by its largest term up to a constant factor when a is bounded away from 1.

known.name: Telescoping sums
known.gloss: A sum of consecutive differences Σ (x_{j+1} − x_j) that collapses to its last term minus its first.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer integer multiplication that replaces four half-size products by three, giving O(n^{log₂3}) time.

known.name: Stacks
known.gloss: A last-in first-out store whose items are removed in reverse order of insertion, as used to save and restore state around recursive calls.

known.name: Binary counter and amortized increment cost
known.gloss: Incrementing a binary counter L times costs O(L) bit flips in total, because bit j flips only about L/2^j times.

known.name: Radix sort and stable sorting
known.gloss: Sorting records by integer keys one digit at a time from least significant to most significant, using a stable pass that preserves the order of equal digits, in time linear in the records times the number of key digits.

known.name: Row-major order and matrix transposition
known.gloss: Storing a matrix row by row so entry (i, j) of an n₁×n₂ matrix sits at position n₂i + j; transposition moves it to position n₁j + i.

known.name: Directed graphs
aliases: head and tail of an edge
known.gloss: Sets of vertices joined by ordered edges, each edge running from its tail to its head.

known.name: Sets, Cartesian products and indicator vectors
known.gloss: Basic set notation, including the product A × B of ordered pairs and the 0/1 vector of a subset of a ground set marking which elements it contains.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The number of k-element subsets of an n-element set, n!/(k!(n−k)!).

known.name: Permutations and cycle notation
known.gloss: Bijections of a finite set to itself, composed as functions, written as products of cycles, with an involution being a permutation equal to its own inverse.

known.name: Union bound
known.gloss: The size (or probability) of a union of sets is at most the sum of their sizes (or probabilities).

known.name: Greatest common divisor and Euclid's algorithm
known.gloss: The largest common divisor of two integers, computed by repeated division, whose extended form also yields Bézout coefficients and hence inverses modulo a coprime modulus.

known.name: Prime numbers and trial division
known.gloss: Integers greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and themselves, testable by checking for divisors up to the square root.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s₁,…,s_d, an integer modulo their product is determined uniquely by its residues modulo each sᵢ, and every choice of residues occurs.

known.name: Matrix operations
known.gloss: Products and inverses of matrices together with their special shapes: identity, diagonal, permutation, upper or lower triangular, and block-diagonal combinations of maps on separate coordinates.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix by adding multiples of one row to another, swapping rows and scaling, which factors any invertible matrix into elementary matrices and computes rank.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The sum Σ xᵢyᵢ of coordinatewise products, with two vectors called orthogonal when it vanishes.

known.name: Projection onto a subspace
known.gloss: The linear map that is the identity on a subspace U and zero on a chosen complementary subspace, so P² = P and its rank is dim U.

known.name: Eigenvalues of a matrix
known.gloss: Scalars λ for which Av = λv has a nonzero solution v; a symmetric matrix is invertible exactly when no eigenvalue is zero.

known.name: Complex conjugate
known.gloss: The map a + bi ↦ a − bi, which preserves modulus and turns e^{iθ} into e^{−iθ}.

known.name: Triangle inequality
known.gloss: The modulus (or norm) of a sum is at most the sum of the moduli.

known.name: Bernoulli's inequality
known.gloss: For x ≥ −1 and integer n ≥ 1, (1 + x)^n ≥ 1 + nx, with strict inequality when x ≠ 0 and n ≥ 2.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: Solving f(x) = 0 by iterating x ↦ x − f(x)/f′(x), whose error roughly squares at each step near a simple root, giving the reciprocal update x(2 − cx) and the square-root update (x + c/x)/2.

known.name: Proof by induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all n by checking a base case and showing each case implies the next, as with invariants maintained by every step of a loop.
